{"body":"## Summary
`entire agent add/list/remove` omitted external agents (e.g. `zed`), failing with `Unknown agent`, even though `entire enable --agent <name>` and the git-hook paths worked. The `agent` noun-group never invoked external-agent discovery, so `agent.Get` / `agent.List` only saw statically-registered built-ins.

Fixes #1928.

## Changes
- `add` / `remove` `RunE`: resolve the single named plugin via the shared `resolveNamedExternalAgent` helper (`external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, name)`) before `agent.Get` / `runRemoveAgent`. Targeting the exact name (rather than a full `$PATH` scan) avoids executing every unrelated `entire-agent-*` binary, and surfaces a real plugin load error instead of a generic "unknown agent". Built-in names short-circuit instantly (no exec); an unknown name still falls through to `printWrongAgentError`. These bypass the `external_agents` gate because the action is itself the opt-in — and `add` auto-persists `external_agents=true` for an external agent (via `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`).
- `entire agent list`: **default lists built-in agents only** — no `$PATH` scan and no plugin exec, so the listing stays fast regardless of how many `entire-agent-*` binaries are on `$PATH`.
  - Because that view is partial, it **says so**: the header is `Built-in agents:` (not the `--external` view's `Agents:`), and the footer reports when the repo has `external_agents` enabled but is not showing those plugins. Without this, the user who had just run `entire agent add <plugin>` — which turns the gate on — got a listing under a completeness-implying header that silently excluded the agent they had installed, and an empty state reading `No built-in agents installed.`
  - Reading the setting for that footer is one file read and no plugin exec, so the no-scan guarantee is unchanged (`TestRunAgentList_DefaultPathDoesNotScanPath` still passes untouched). The alternative — having the default path honour the gate and discover — was rejected deliberately: `entire agent list` would then change both cost and content off a setting the user never typed.
- **`--external`** is a **superset**: it lists the built-in agents *and* the external plugins on `$PATH` (installed and available) via full discovery, reusing the built-in rendering — installed `✓` marker, sort order, and test-only filter — so the two views differ only where they must (its header is unscoped, and it is the view whose empty state can honestly say `No agents installed.`). External entries carry an `(external)` suffix, because they are arbitrary executables resolved from `$PATH` rather than code shipped in the binary, and that distinction is trust-relevant.
  - This replaces the earlier `--all` flag. Previously the default path executed every plugin on `$PATH` to mark installed externals — a per-plugin exec cost that scaled with plugin count on a sub-100ms command. All external work is now behind the explicit `--external` opt-in.
- Discovery lives in the run function (not the group's `PersistentPreRunE`), so unit tests calling `runAgentList` directly exercise it.
- **`printAgentError` (the "Unknown agent" / "Missing agent name" path) no longer contradicts `agent list`**:
  - It goes through the new `agent.ListAvailable`, so test-only agents (`vogon`) are no longer advertised as available.
  - The trailing hint now follows one rule: **it exists only to cover a listing that is knowably incomplete.** What the caller did about `$PATH` before giving up on the name decides which hint, if any, is honest.
    - A full `$PATH` scan already ran, so the listing is complete → **no hint**. This is `enable --agent`, which runs `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` at `setup.go:892` fourteen lines before the failing `agent.Get`: every plugin is already in the listing, marked `(external)`, so pointing at `entire agent list --external` sent the user to repeat a search whose results were four lines above.
    - A targeted single-name lookup ran → `externalAgentSearchedHint(name)`, which names the one plugin that came up missing. This is `agent add` / `agent remove`.
    - No lookup at all → `externalAgentHint`, now down to exactly one caller: the `--agent` `FlagErrorFunc`, which cobra invokes during flag parsing, before `enable`'s `RunE` and so before its scan.
    - `printMissingAgentError` was reached from both sides of that line, so it splits into `…PreDiscovery` / `…PostDiscovery`. `printAgentError` treats an empty hint as omit, with no stray blank line left behind.
  - The usage line follows the caller's command surface (`entire agent add` / `entire agent remove` / `entire enable --agent`) instead of always printing `entire enable --agent`.
- **New `agent.ListAvailable() []ResolvedAgent`** is the single place the test-only filter lives; `StringList`, `runAgentList`, `printAgentError`, and `hookAgentOptions` (the interactive agent picker, which carried its own inline `TestOnly` check) all go through it, so "which agents are available" has one answer across the command surface. No inline test-only checks remain outside `registry.go`. It returns name+agent pairs because an external plugin's self-reported `Name()` is not validated against the registry key derived from its binary, and the registry key is the identity users type and `agent.Get` accepts.
  - `agent.Get`'s unknown-agent error was the last unfiltered user-facing listing — `main.go` prints it verbatim where a command doesn't intercept it, and it named `vogon`. It now lists `StringList()`, with the read lock released before the message is formatted so `StringList` (which resolves each agent through `Get`) can't re-enter `registryMu`. That also removes the latent nested `RLock` the old `List()` call had on that line.
  - The pre-existing `List` and `StringList` keep their names. `List` stays deliberately unfiltered because the registry's own plumbing needs every registered name: `hooks_cmd.go` builds the `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` subcommands from it and the Vogon binary invokes `entire hooks vogon <verb>`, so filtering there would break every canary test; `external/discovery.go` needs the full set to avoid re-registering a name already taken. Renaming these for clarity is a separate concern and stays out of this PR.
- **New `agent.IsRegistered`** for existence probes. `external/discovery.go` was asking "is this name taken?" by discarding a `Get` error, which built the whole `available: ...` listing (resolving every registered agent) just to answer yes/no.
- `agent.SnapshotForTesting` moved to `cmd/entire/cli/agent/testing.go` — it cannot live in a `_test.go` because package `cli`'s tests need it, and the filename follows `internal/entireclient/tokenstore/testing.go`, the existing precedent for a dedicated cross-package test-helper file. Its doc comment is narrowed: capture/restore are safe against concurrent registry *readers*, not writers, since restore replaces the whole map.
- Docs: `docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md` claimed discovery "runs once during CLI initialization". There is no such step — every call site is inside a command, in one of three shapes (gated full scan, ungated full scan, ungated single-name lookup). The Discovery section now documents which commands use which, that `external_agents` gates the first, and how `agent list` and `--external` differ. `CLAUDE.md`'s command-layout entry for `agent` gained the same `list` / `list --external` / `add`-`remove` distinction.
- Drive-by, unrelated to external agents: `agent/architecture_test.go` had `//nolint:staticcheck` separated from the `parser.ParseDir` call by another comment line, where the directive does not apply. Moved onto the offending line.

## Test
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagListsAvailablePlugin`: the default listing does not surface an available external plugin; `--external` lists it.
- `TestRunAgentList_DefaultPathDoesNotScanPath`: asserts on an exec log the mock plugin appends to, proving the default path never execs a plugin while `--external` does — the guarantee the filter-driven absence check above cannot make.
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalFlagMarksInstalled`: `--external` lists an installed external plugin marked `✓`.
- `TestRunAgentList_ExternalIsSuperset`: `--external` includes both the external plugin and the built-ins.
- `TestRunAgentList_MarksExternalProvenance`: external lines carry `(external)`, built-in lines do not.
- `TestRunAgentList_HeaderScopedToMode`: the default header scopes itself to built-ins; `--external`, the complete view, does not.
- `TestRunAgentList_DefaultFooterNamesEnabledGate`: with `external_agents` on, the default listing reports the plugins it is omitting; with the gate unset it prints the plain `--external` pointer and does not claim the gate is on.
- `TestRunAgentList_EmptyStateWording`: mode-scoped empty state — "No built-in agents installed" by default, "No agents installed" under `--external`.
- `TestEnableCmd_UnknownAgent_ListsPluginsAndOmitsHint` executes the real `enable` `RunE` with a mock plugin on `$PATH` and asserts the plugin appears marked `(external)` **and** that no hint follows. This is the test that had to exist: the pre-existing unit test passed only because it called `printWrongAgentError` directly with the hint hardcoded, never triggering the discovery that made the hint wrong. Verified red by reverting just the `enable` call site.
- `TestPrintAgentError_ExcludesTestOnlyAgents`, `TestPrintAgentError_PointsAtExternalListing`, `TestPrintAgentError_HintReflectsWhatWasSearched` (inverted: after a full scan, neither hint wording may appear, and no doubled blank line), `TestAgentAdd_UnknownNameReportsSearchedPath`, and the usage-line assertion in `TestPrintWrongAgentError` cover the error-path fixes.
- `TestSnapshotForTesting_RestoresRegistry` covers the registry snapshot helper; `TestIsRegistered` pins that the probe answers for test-only agents too, since it reports registry membership rather than user-facing availability.
- `TestGet_UnknownAgentErrorExcludesTestOnly` pins that `Get`'s error lists real agents and not test-only ones (verified red before green; the package also passes under `-race`, since the fix changes locking).
- The external-plugin tests share one `withExternalAgentPlugin` helper (isolated repo, `#!/bin/sh` mock plugin on a scrubbed `$PATH`, registry snapshot/restore), parameterised on the two axes that actually differ: whether the mock reports its hooks installed, and whether the settings enable `external_agents` — the listing tests opt in, `add`/`remove` deliberately leave it unset because naming a plugin is itself the opt-in. They skip when no POSIX shell is available.

## Verification
- `mise run fmt` — clean
- `mise run lint` (golangci-lint 2.11.3) — 0 issues
- `mise run test:ci` — PASS
- Benchmark (9 shell plugins on `$PATH`, `external_agents:true`): default `agent list` **18 execs → 0**; external listing moved behind `--external`. Wall clock for the opt-in path, min of 6 runs: default 1.13s vs `--external` 1.69s, i.e. ~60ms per plugin for the two subcommands discovery invokes.

Code-review finding on PR #1930 (branch fix/1928-agent-group-external-discovery, repo /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/pr-reviews). Please fix it and ship it (commit + push + update the PR), then report back to me.

Finding — cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go:152 (low severity):

`resolveNamedExternalAgent` promotes `discoverAndRegisterNamed`'s validation error into a hard command failure, so a mistyped name containing a path separator bypasses the friendly error path entirely. `entire agent add ./claude-code` (or a completion artifact like `bin/claude-code`) prints the raw:

    loading external agent "./claude-code": invalid external agent name "./claude-code": contains path separators

instead of the `Unknown agent …` message plus the available-agents listing and usage line that every other bad name gets. Same applies to `exec.ErrDot`, which `discoverAndRegisterNamed` also propagates as a non-`ErrNotFound` error when `.` is on `$PATH`.

Suggested fix: treat the path-separator case and `exec.ErrDot` as "no plugin by that name" — fall through to `printWrongAgentError` so the miss path stays uniform across `agent add` and `agent remove`. Keep genuine plugin *load* failures as hard errors (that distinction was deliberate in this PR).

Please add a test covering `entire agent add ./<name>` producing the friendly unknown-agent output. Follow the repo checklist before pushing: `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` (note: use the mise-installed golangci-lint directly if a stale v1 shadows it).

When done, SendMessage back to "cli-d4" with what you changed and the commit/push result.

content.text:
Pulled up the code. Here's how I'd think about it.

## What's actually broken

`Get`'s miss path formats `available: %v` from `StringList()` → `ListAvailable()` → `Get(name)` for every registered name. So `Get` can call itself. Two separate smells in one:

1. **Mutual recursion.** In practice it bottoms out at depth 2 — the inner `Get` calls are on names just read out of the map, so they hit. It only goes deeper if entries keep vanishing mid-loop. So this is a latent cleanup, not a live bug (severity is right at "low").
2. **`ListAvailable` uses an error-returning lookup and throws the error away** — paying a full registry re-resolution to build a string it discards. That's the part I'd actually call wrong regardless of recursion.

There's a third thing hiding underneath: `ListAvailable` takes `RLock` N+1 times (once in `List`, once per `Get`), so it reads a **torn view** of the registry. That's why the doc comment has to explain a "vanishes between listing and resolving" case at all — the caveat exists only because the read is two-phase.

## The two fixes

**Minimal — unexported non-erroring lookup:**

```go
func lookup(name types.AgentName) (Agent, bool) {
	registryMu.RLock()
	factory, ok := registry[name]
	registryMu.RUnlock()
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	return factory(), nil
}
```

`Get` becomes `lookup` + error formatting; `ListAvailable`, `DetectAll`, and `AgentForTranscriptPath` (all three do the same `List` → `Get` → discard-error dance) switch to `lookup`. Recursion gone, ~4 lines net.

**Better — snapshot once:**

```go
// entries returns name→factory pairs in sorted name order, captured under a
// single read lock so callers see one consistent view of the registry.
func entries() []struct{ name types.AgentName; factory Factory }
```

`ListAvailable` then loops over the snapshot and calls `factory()` outside the lock. This kills the recursion *and* deletes the skip-on-error branch and the tear-window paragraph in the doc comment — the case stops being possible instead of being documented. `DetectAll` and `AgentForTranscriptPath` get the same treatment.

I checked the factories are safe to call in that loop: external ones are `func() agent.Agent { return wrapped }` over an already-wrapped value (`external/discovery.go:230`), built-ins just construct a struct. No exec, no I/O — which is also why calling them outside the lock costs nothing.

**I'd go with the snapshot.** The minimal version fixes the recursion but leaves `ListAvailable` documenting a race it doesn't need to have. content.text:
In the listing/selection path, four properties get asked about an agent — and they're asked in three structurally different ways, which is the interesting part:

**1. `IsTestOnly()` — optional interface, type-asserted**
`TestOnly` (`agent.go:356`) embeds `Agent` and adds `IsTestOnly() bool`. Probed at `registry.go:101` via `ag.(TestOnly)`. Post-#1930 this is the *only* place it's asked — that was the point of `ListAvailable`. Free: no I/O.

**2. `external.IsExternal(ag)` — not a method at all**
`capabilities.go:153` is a type switch on the wrapper types (`*wrappedAgent`, `*wrappedAgentWithProtectedFiles`). Provenance isn't something an agent self-reports — deliberately, since an external plugin could just lie. Drives the `(external)` suffix and the default-view filter. Free.

**3. `hooksInstalled(ctx, ag)` — optional interface + I/O**
`config.go:105`: `agent.AsHookSupport(ag)` then `AreHooksInstalled(ctx)`. This is the expensive one — for an external agent it's a plugin exec, which is exactly the cost `--external` gates. Note the ordering in `runAgentList`: the `isExternal` filter `continue`s *before* `hooksInstalled` is called, which is what makes the no-exec guarantee hold.

**4. `IsPreview()` — required method on the core `Agent` interface**
`agent.go:36`, so every agent must answer. But `agent list` never asks: the only consumers are `setup.go:2027` and `:2033`, the interactive picker. So the listing shows a `✓` for installed and `(external)` for provenance, and silently drops the preview/stable distinction that the picker surfaces.

That asymmetry is worth naming: three of the four axes are consulted by the listing, and the one that's a *mandatory* part of the interface is the one it ignores. `entire agent add codex` from the picker tells you it's preview; `entire agent list` doesn't. Not in scope for #1930, but it's the same class of "the listing doesn't say what it knows" problem that PR spent its `Built-in agents:`/footer work fixing.

Sidebar on **#3**: this reinforces the snapshot approach. All four probes want an `Agent` *value*, so any fix has to keep handing out constructed agents — `ListAvailable` returning `ResolvedAgent` is right, and a one-shot `entries()` snapshot feeds those probes from a single consistent view instead of N separate `Get` calls. Your scope question there is still open.

content.text:
Direct answer to the literal question first, then the pushback — because I think the speed premise doesn't survive contact with the code.

## What listing/help actually consults

| Property | `agent list` | `printAgentError` / `StringList` | picker (`setup.go`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| registry key | ✓ | ✓ (only thing it prints) | ✓ |
| `IsTestOnly()` | ✓ (filter) | ✓ (filter) | ✓ (filter) |
| `IsExternal(ag)` | ✓ (filter + suffix) | — | — |
| `AreHooksInstalled(ctx)` | ✓ (the `✓` marker) | — | ✓ |
| `IsPreview()` | — | — | ✓ |
| `Description()` | — | — | ✓ |

So the error/help listings need **name + test-only** and nothing else. `agent list` adds provenance and installed-state.

## Why the descriptor won't make it faster

The descriptor you're describing already exists — it's `external.Agent.info`. Look at `external/external.go:64-78`: `Name()`, `Type()`, `Description()`, `IsPreview()` are all plain field reads off a struct captured at registration. **Every descriptive property is already zero-exec after Register.** There's nothing left to precompute.

And the factories are trivial: external registers `func() agent.Agent { return wrapped }` over the already-built wrapper (`discovery.go:230`), built-ins construct a struct. So `ListAvailable` calling `factory()` N times costs approximately nothing.

The two execs per plugin the PR benchmarked (18 for 9 plugins) are:

1. **`info` at registration** — that's *how* the descriptor gets populated. A register-time descriptor can't avoid it; it's the source.
2. **`are-hooks-installed` at list time** (`external.go:286`) — and this one is **mutable repo state**, not a property of the agent. It changes when the user runs `agent add`, edits settings files, switches worktrees. Caching it at Register makes `agent list` show stale `✓` markers. It's the one probe that genuinely must be live.

"Penalize register instead" is the part that doesn't land: registration *is* the expensive half. #1930's fix wasn't to make registration cheaper — it was to not register at all unless you ask (`--external`).

## What would actually buy the speed

Cache the plugin `info` **on disk**, keyed by binary path + mtime + size, under `userdirs.Cache()`. That kills exec #1 across invocations — the repeated `--external` run goes from 9 execs to 0, and only a changed/new binary pays. That's the real ~60ms/plugin, and it's a legitimately good idea. Invalidation is honest (mtime+size on the binary you're about to trust anyway), and it composes with the gate rather than replacing it.

Exec #2 stays live. You could shave it to one exec by folding installed-state into a single `describe` call, but that's a protocol change to `external-agent-protocol.md` and a compat break for existing plugins — separate conversation.

## Where the descriptor idea *is* right

Not for speed — for correctness and clarity:

- It fixes **#3** properly. A `map[AgentName]registration{descriptor, factory}` lets `entries()` return descriptors under one `RLock` with no `factory()` calls and no torn view. The `Get`-recursion and the "vanishes between listing and resolving" caveat both evaporate.
- `printAgentError`/`StringList` stop instantiating agents just to read a name and a bool.
- `IsTestOnly` and `IsExternal` become **declared at the registration site** instead of an interface assertion and a type switch on wrapper types.

One hard constraint on that last point: `External` must be set by the *registrar*, not read from the plugin's `info`. Provenance is a trust signal, and a plugin that self-reports `external: false` would launder itself into looking built-in. `IsExternal`'s type switch is ugly but unforgeable; a descriptor field is only as safe as the one line in `discovery.go` that sets it.

My read: do the descriptor for #3's sake and take the clarity win, state plainly in the commit that it's not a perf change, and file the disk-backed `info` cache as the actual perf work. Want me to sketch the descriptor shape against the current `registry.go`?

No — as an addition it makes the code bigger. Here's the ledger, with real counts.

**What it deletes:**
- One type assertion (`registry.go:101` — the *only* `TestOnly)` assertion outside tests)
- `ListAvailable`'s skip-on-error branch, ~3 lines, plus its doc caveat

**What it adds:**
- A descriptor type + `registration{descriptor, factory}` struct
- A `Register` signature change across **9 built-in call sites** + the external one, plus test registrations — or a second `RegisterWithDescriptor` entry point, which is worse (two registration paths to keep in sync)
- **The real cost: a parallel description channel.** Every built-in would declare `Name`/`Type`/`Description`/`IsPreview`/test-only *twice* — once as interface methods (still required, because the picker, `hooks_cmd.go`, and the hook plumbing hold `Agent` values, not registry keys) and once in the descriptor. Two sources of truth that can silently drift.

And `IsExternal` doesn't go away. It has **11 non-test callers**, and 10 of them (`setup.go`, `explain_summary_provider.go`, `explain.go`, `manual_commit_condensation.go`) hold a bare `agent.Agent` obtained from `getSummaryAgent` or a setup flow — they have a *value*, not a registry name, so a descriptor keyed by name can't serve them. The type switch stays either way. Only `agent_group.go:95` could switch.

So: −1 assertion, −3 lines, +10 touched call sites and a drift risk. That's not simplification.

**Compare the plain `entries()` snapshot for #3:** ~10 lines inside `registry.go`, deletes the same skip branch and the same caveat, fixes the recursion, changes **zero call sites outside the file**. Strictly smaller and it solves the thing that's actually wrong.

---

There *is* a version of your idea that genuinely simplifies, and it's the more radical one: make descriptive identity registry **data instead of agent behavior** — delete `Name()`, `Type()`, `Description()`, `IsPreview()` from the `Agent` interface (4 of the 6 methods in its identity block) and let the registration carry them. No duplication, because the methods stop existing. That's coherent, and the interface gets meaningfully thinner.

But it's a refactor across 12 agent implementations plus the external wrapper, and it touches the protocol doc. Wrong thing to land inside a bug-fix PR that's already 25 commits deep — and per your own isolated-PRs rule, it's its own objective.

My recommendation: `entries()` snapshot for #3 now, and if the descriptor appeals, do it as the interface-thinning version in its own PR where the payoff is real.

# External Agent Plugin Protocol

## Overview

The Entire CLI supports external agent plugins — standalone binaries that implement the Agent interface via a subcommand-based protocol over stdin/stdout. This allows third-party agents to integrate with the CLI without modifying the main repository.

## Discovery

The CLI discovers external agents by scanning `$PATH` for executables matching the pattern `entire-agent-<name>`. For example, `entire-agent-cursor` would register as the "cursor" agent.

- Binaries whose `<name>` conflicts with an already-registered built-in agent are skipped.
- The binary must be executable and respond to the `info` subcommand.

Discovery is **per-command**, not a one-time CLI initialization step: each
command that needs external agents runs it itself, in one of three shapes.

| Entry point | Scope | Gate | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `external.DiscoverAndRegister` | Full `$PATH` scan | Skipped unless `external_agents` is enabled | Most commands: `status`, `review`, `explain`, `resume`, `attach`, `rewind`, the `hooks` command trees, and post-commit condensation |
| `external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` | Full `$PATH` scan | Bypassed | Interactive setup flows and `entire agent list --external` |
| `external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` | Looks up `entire-agent-<name>` only | Bypassed | `entire agent add` / `entire agent remove` |

Consequences worth knowing:

- The `external_agents` setting gates discovery. With it off, a full scan is
  skipped entirely and external agents are invisible to the gated commands.
- The `…Always` variants bypass that gate because the user's action *is* the
  opt-in. `entire agent add <external-name>` therefore auto-persists
  `external_agents: true`, so the hooks it installs are still resolvable on
  later, gated runs.
- The named variant executes only the plugin being addressed, so `entire agent
  add`/`remove` never run unrelated `entire-agent-*` binaries, and a plugin
  that fails to load surfaces its real error rather than a generic
  "unknown agent".
- `entire agent list` lists built-in agents only and performs no scan;
  `entire agent list --external` is the superset — built-ins plus the plugins
  found on `$PATH`, with external entries marked `(external)`.

## Environment

=== FINDING 1 (medium) — docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md, the new "Entry point / Scope / Gate / Used by" table (~line 19) ===

The table's "Used by" column is wrong in one place and incomplete in two. I enumerated the real call sites with grep — these are verified, use them rather than re-deriving:

`external.DiscoverAndRegister` row currently claims: "Most commands: `status`, `review`, `explain`, `resume`, `attach`, `rewind`, the `hooks` command trees, and post-commit condensation".
- WRONG: `status` does no external discovery at all. `cmd/entire/cli/status.go` has no `external` import and no discovery call; its agent listing goes `InstalledAgentDisplayNames` → `agent.List()`. Drop it. (This is exactly the class of stale claim the PR set out to remove — cf. the deleted "runs once during CLI initialization".)
- Correct and verified callers: resume.go:66, checkpoint_resume.go:69, trail_resume_cmd.go:165, attach.go:112, review/cmd.go:165, rewind.go:77, explain.go:1112, hooks_cmd.go:48, hooks_git_cmd.go:178, strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:39 (post-commit condensation — that part of the claim is accurate), and explain_summary_provider.go:29 (the summary-provider lookup, currently unmentioned).

`external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` row currently claims: "Interactive setup flows and `entire agent list --external`". It omits the two NON-interactive users, and one of them matters for this PR's own reasoning:
- setup.go:892 — `entire enable --agent <name>`. This is the full scan that the PR's whole "no hint after a full scan" rule depends on. It must be in the table.
- setup.go:206 — `entire configure --summarize-provider`.
- (setup.go:408/472/495 are the interactive setup flows already covered by the existing wording; agent_group.go:80 is the `--external` listing.)

`external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` row currently claims: "`entire agent add` / `entire agent remove`". It omits `entire dispatch`'s summary-provider lookup, via the `discoverDispatchSummaryProvider` indirection at explain_summary_provider.go:31.

Please keep the table's shape; just make the "Used by" cells true. Naming representative commands rather than exhaustive file lists is fine, but `status` must go and `enable --agent` must appear.

=== FINDING 2 (low/medium) — cmd/entire/cli/agent/testing.go:31 ===

`SnapshotForTesting`'s returned `restore` closure does `registry = snapshot` — it assigns the snapshot map itself rather than copying back into a fresh map. So restore is not repeatable: after the first call the package-global `registry` *is* `snapshot`, any later `Register` mutates the snapshot, and a second `restore()` is a no-op.

That's not hypothetical — it's the shape of the PR's own new test `TestSnapshotForTesting_RestoresRegistry`, which registers `restore` with `t.Cleanup` AND calls it directly. Sequence: `restore := SnapshotForTesting(); t.Cleanup(restore); ...; restore(); agent.Register("mock", ...)` — the cleanup then leaves `mock` in the registry. Since these mocks are backed by `t.TempDir` binaries, a later test's `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` can exec a deleted file. Registry leakage across tests is the exact thing this helper was added to prevent.

Fix: clone inside the returned closure, e.g. `registry = maps.Clone(snapshot)`.

Also update the doc comment: it promises restore returns the registry "to exactly that state" and only excepts concurrent *writers*. Repeat-restore is a second caveat that the fix removes — so the comment should stop needing it, not document it.

Please add a test that calls `restore()` twice with a `Register` in between and asserts the second restore still clears it.

Checklist before pushing, as before: `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` (mise-installed golangci-lint direct). Report back to "cli-d4" with what changed and the commit/push result.

input.command: cd /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/pr-reviews; grep -n "isBuiltInAgent" cmd/entire/cli/*.go | grep -v _test; echo "=== detectOrSelectAgent ==="; grep -n "func detectOrSelectAgent" cmd/entire/cli/setup.go

content.text:
Your read is right, and the naming is the reason it's confusing. Two different questions:

- **`ListAvailable`** — "is this agent *addressable*?" Registry membership minus test-only. Free.
- **`DetectAll`** — "does this agent look *configured in this repo*?" Calls `DetectPresence(ctx)` on each, which for a built-in stats for `.claude`/`.gemini`, and for an external plugin is an **exec** of its `detect-presence` subcommand.

So detection is a superset question layered on availability: you must be available to be detected.

## The two `isBuiltInAgent` filters

`isBuiltInAgent` is just `!external.IsExternal(ag)` (`setup.go:1823`), and it's used in exactly two places in `detectOrSelectAgent`:

**`setup.go:1772` — preselection. This one is defensible.** On first run, detected built-ins get pre-ticked; detected externals don't. Detection for an external plugin means *the plugin's own exec said "yes, enable me"* — and pre-ticking it means hooks get installed on confirm. Trusting a `$PATH` executable's self-assertion to auto-enroll itself is a different trust decision from trusting shipped code. The plugin still appears in the picker, just unchecked, so the user opts in by ticking. That's the same philosophy as the `external_agents` gate and the `(external)` marker.

**`setup.go:1722` — the announcement. This one I can't justify, and I think it's a mistake.** It suppresses `Detected agent: X` when the single detected agent is external. But printing a line is *information*, not consent — and the branch right below it (`len(detected) > 1`, line 1726) doesn't filter at all, so it happily announces external agents by name. Net effect: one detected external → silent; two detected including an external → announced. Same fact, opposite behavior, based only on how many other agents you happen to have. Looks like the filter was pasted onto both sites when only the preselection one had a reason.

## "That list should be the same as `entire agent list`"

Post-#1930 it is — same source. The picker's `hookAgentOptions` (`setup.go:436`) calls `agent.ListAvailable()`, and so does `runAgentList`. That was the point of the "one answer to which agents are available" commit. Setup runs `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways`, so the picker's set matches **`agent list --external`** (not the default built-ins-only view). Remaining intentional difference: the picker also drops agents without `HookSupport` (`setup.go:439`), since you can't install hooks for them.

But there's a gap you'll care about, and it's the same defect this PR just fixed in the listing: **the picker doesn't mark provenance.** Line 442 labels each option with `ra.Agent.Type()` and nothing else. So in `entire enable`, an external `$PATH` executable renders identically to a shipped built-in — no `(external)`. The PR argued at length that this distinction is trust-relevant and added the suffix to both `agent list --external` and `printAgentError`. The picker is the third surface, it's the one where ticking the box *installs hooks*, and it's the one still silent about it.

## Scope call on #3

Leave `DetectAll` out. Its only caller is `detectOrSelectAgent`, it runs once per setup, and its cost is `DetectPresence` execs — not the `Get` loop. Fixing the loop there buys nothing measurable, and touching it drags setup's behavior into a registry cleanup. **Keep #3 to `ListAvailable` + `entries()`**, which is where the recursion actually matters.

Two new items from this, both small and both arguably in scope for a PR about agent listings:

1. `setup.go:1722` — drop the `isBuiltInAgent` guard on the announcement (or apply it to the multi-agent branch too, but I'd just drop it).
2. `setup.go:442` — add the `(external)` suffix to picker options, matching `agent list --external` and `printAgentError`.

Want me to send those to `fix-agent-list` as well, or hold them for a follow-up PR?
